subject: Throughput playtest results & next configuration steps
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@fleetai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Donovan <claire@fleetai.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Quick recap from today's playtest + ask

Thanks for running the playtest today — quick recap and two asks. Attached is our CSV export (fleetai_playtest_summary.csv) and a small sample of request traces (sample-request-traces.jsonl).

What we observed on our side:
- Steady baseline: ~12 QPS (production-like steady traffic) with average request size ~420 tokens (median 380, 90th 720).
- Short spikes: repeated short bursts (20–45s) up to ~40 QPS, likely from user refresh patterns.
- Single heavier crest: a ~3-minute burst that reached 180 QPS (one-off campaign burst).
- Streaming use case: up to ~120 concurrent streaming sessions during peak minutes; those sessions emit ~12 tokens/sec each on average.
- End-to-end latency we measure from client: P95 for normal completions ~420ms during steady; P95 jumps to ~1.2s during the 3-minute crest.

Two asks: can you (1) confirm what Redwood would recommend for a configuration that meets a P95 <= 300ms goal for normal completions (steady + typical short spikes), and (2) propose fallback/rollout options for the crest behavior so we avoid a service interruption during marketing bursts?

Also FYI, we ran a small experiment with prefix caching for repeated user prompts — it helped for ~15% of calls but didn't materially change peak tail during the crest.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Platform Engineering, FleetAI
attachments: fleetai_playtest_summary.csv, sample-request-traces.jsonl

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@fleetai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 19:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick recap from today's playtest + ask

Thanks for the clear notes and the artifacts, Samir — super helpful. A few clarifying questions before we provide a sizing rec:  

1) Request size distribution: you gave median/90th which is perfect. Can you also share the percentage of requests <=128 tokens and <=256 tokens? That helps us decide routing to smaller model variants.

2) Burst shape: the 3-minute crest is the main risk. Do you have histograms for inter-arrival during that crest (even coarse buckets like 0–100ms, 100–500ms, >500ms)? We want to understand if it’s many concurrent short requests or a smaller set of long-lived streaming sessions.

3) Streaming SLA: do you need strict per-event latency (e.g., 95th <= 500ms for each emitted event), or is overall session responsiveness acceptable if occasional events are slower?

Initial thoughts (high level):
- Given steady ~12 QPS and median ~380 tokens, baseline tokens/sec ≈ 4.5k. Peaks up to 180 QPS push tokens/sec much higher (~75–80k) depending on token size. The delta between steady and crest suggests we should avoid relying on a single small reserve — routing + autoscale + temporary capacity bump will be needed.
- A multi-pronged approach usually works: route short requests to a small/efficient model, reserve a base pool for steady traffic, and configure burst capacity (either dedicated extra pods or hosted overflow to a cheaper variant) with an automatic fallback policy.

Next step proposal: Monica (cc'd) will draft a concrete sizing scenario (pods/target tokens/sec, expected P95) and a short canary plan. If that looks good, we can schedule a short stress window (30–60 minutes) where you run the crest again while we trace from the Redwood side. That will let us validate tail behavior under real traffic.

If you can answer 1–3 above and confirm a 48–72h window when you can reproduce a crest, we'll prepare the canary config.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@fleetai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:45:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Quick recap from today's playtest + ask — concrete sizing scenarios + actions

Appended is a short matrix (inline below) and I've attached two artifacts: a tuned config template and the pod-sizing estimate based on today's traffic. Attachments: fleetai_playtest_summary.csv (from you), sample-request-traces.jsonl (from you), plus our config template (redwood_playtest_config.yaml).

High-level sizing scenarios (P95 target <= 300ms for non-streaming completions):

Scenario A — Conservative (short-term, hosted/dedicated hybrid)
- Baseline provision: capacity for 15 QPS @ median 380 tokens (~5.7k tokens/sec) to guarantee headroom for steady spikes.
- Burst reserve: on-demand pool to absorb up to additional 50 QPS for short spikes (20–60s) using compatible model variant (slightly quantized for cost) — expected aggregate tokens/sec headroom ~25k.
- Expected P95 (steady + short spikes): <= 300ms for completions <512 tokens.
- Pros: low upfront commit; Cons: may still see tail degradation during the 3-minute crest.

Scenario B — Guarded (recommended for near-term stability)
- Baseline provision: capacity for 25 QPS @ median 380 tokens (~9.5k tokens/sec).
- Burst reserve: dedicated autoscale group to climb to handle an extra 120 QPS for short periods (configured to scale over 30–60s), target aggregate tokens/sec ~60–80k during crest.
- Canaries: route 10% of traffic during crest to a cheaper model variant as a fallback.
- Expected P95 (steady + crest with autoscale): <= 350ms; with canary routing and rapid autoscale tuning we expect to meet <=300ms most runs.
- Pros: more robust for marketing bursts; Cons: higher reserved cost or multi-minute autoscale hysteresis risk.

Streaming guidance (concurrent sessions up to 120)
- Treat streaming sessions separately: provision conversational workers that optimize for low per-event latency. For 120 concurrent streams emitting ~12 tokens/sec, budget ~1.5k tokens/sec dedicated to streaming plus headroom for bursts.
- Recommend separate SLOs for streaming event latency (P95 <= 500ms). If strict per-event guarantees are required, we should isolate streaming pods.

Operational recommendations / immediate next steps
- Action: Samir to provide token-count histogram buckets for <=128 and <=256 tokens and coarse inter-arrival histogram for the crest. (Owner: Samir) — due EOD Mon 2026-11-15
- Action: Redwood (Monica + Karthik) to prepare redwood_playtest_config.yaml and a canary run playbook for a 60-minute stress window. (Owner: Monica) — initial draft by 2026-11-14
- Action: Schedule a 60-minute stress window where FleetAI reproduces the crest. Redwood will collect traces and produce a tail-latency report within 24h after the run. (Owner: all) — target window 48–72h after confirmations.

Fallback / rollout ideas
- Canary route 10–20% of traffic to a cheaper quantized variant during the crest (quick circuit-breaker).
- Progressive ramp: if autoscale cannot keep up, degrade non-essential features (e.g., higher-resolution outputs) to preserve core completion latency.

If this looks reasonable I'll convert Scenario B into a concrete pod-by-pod estimate and include a short cost delta. We can also set up a short trial of dedicated capacity so you can validate economics on a real crest.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_playtest_config.yaml, fleetai_pod_sizing_estimate.pdf
